text: A computer-implemented method for generating a response to a natural-language query, the method comprising: ingesting content received in a plurality of distinct modalities through a corresponding plurality of modality-specific extraction stages, each said extraction stage failing independently of every other said extraction stage; constructing, from an output of at least one said extraction stage, a plurality of knowledge records, each said knowledge record encoding a single semantic assertion as a subject reference, a predicate reference and an object, and each said knowledge record further comprising, within a single record schema, a confidence value maintained as a first parameter accumulating evidence supporting said semantic assertion and a second parameter accumulating evidence contradicting it and reported as a ratio of said first parameter to a sum thereof, a safety classification, a semantic fingerprint computed over a canonicalized form of said semantic assertion, and a reference into a provenance chain; appending, for each said knowledge record, a node to said provenance chain, said provenance chain being append-only and each said node carrying a checksum computed over an operation and a safety evaluation recorded for said operation; receiving a query from a requester; constructing, before traversal of said knowledge records, a scope description bounded by an access entitlement of said requester and by a time interval, such that a knowledge record outside said scope description is not traversable; retrieving from within said scope description a candidate set of said knowledge records; admitting into an admitted set only those knowledge records of said candidate set whose retrieval confidence satisfies a configured threshold; iteratively updating an activation value of each knowledge record of said admitted set as a threshold function of a weighted sum of the activation values of the other knowledge records of said admitted set, until said activation values reach a stable state, and retaining a stabilized set comprising those knowledge records whose activation value is positive at said stable state; constructing a graph structure in which every edge references at least one knowledge record of said stabilized set; generating output text, wherein at each generation step a permissible output vocabulary is constrained to terms derivable from said edges, and wherein a candidate proposition not derivable from said edges is rejected before output in favour of a narrower proposition that is so derivable; and delivering said output text together with a citation resolving each said proposition to at least one knowledge record of said stabilized set.

The method of claim 1, further comprising: receiving an output attributed to an external system; evaluating each factual assertion of said output against said knowledge records; marking each said factual assertion as supported together with a citation to a knowledge record supporting it, or as unsupported; classifying said output against a plurality of categories comprising an untraceable assertion, an assertion exceeding a scope declared for said external system, and a self-contradiction between two assertions of said output; and where said output contains a textual pattern of self-referential language, generating a citation of the specific text observed and generating no output asserting a determination concerning an internal state of said external system.

The method of claim 1, further comprising: registering a connector to an external system, said registering recording a capability declared by said external system, an authentication credential, a data mapping between a representation of said external system and a schema of said knowledge records, and a health-reporting interface; permitting an operation directed to said external system only where said operation is within a said declared capability; and performing said retrieving and said generating identically whether or not any said connector is registered, such that no said external system is a dependency thereof.

The method of claim 1, further comprising generating a plurality of candidate hypotheses by sampling from a distribution in which a selection probability of a candidate is a logistic function of a scored difference between said candidate and an incumbent candidate scaled by an inverse-temperature parameter, wherein each said candidate hypothesis carries a status field set to a proposed state and transitions to a validated state only upon confirmation by an identified human reviewer, no automated process being configured to effect said transition.

The method of claim 1, further comprising: establishing an entitlement of a holder to a work under a licence record; minting a token representation of said entitlement only after said entitlement is so established; transferring said token representation to a wallet controlled by said holder, said token representation being at no time held by a party performing said method; and where a state of said token representation diverges from said entitlement record, presenting said entitlement record as authoritative and recording said divergence.

The method of claim 1, further comprising delivering an audio narration of content by one of a first mechanism reproducing a recorded asset of an identified natural person and a second mechanism synthesizing speech from a voice profile having no derivation from, fitting to, or correspondence with any specific natural person, wherein said first mechanism requires said recorded asset of said identified natural person and no configuration of said second mechanism produces a voice corresponding to a specific natural person.

The method of claim 1, further comprising: analysing a sensor feed under an explicit and revocable authorization of a requester in order to locate an object; classifying an object from a frame of said sensor feed; excluding from a candidate result set every classification result corresponding to a natural person or to an animal, such that no said classification result is surfaced to said requester at any ranking position; and representing a remaining said classification result as a session-scoped record not retained beyond an active session absent a separate explicit election to retain it.

The method of claim 1, further comprising: determining that a confidence value of an inference derived from a plurality of said knowledge records falls below a configured threshold; identifying a knowledge record that, were it present, would raise said confidence value above said threshold; and generating a structured query directed to obtaining said identified knowledge record and presenting said structured query to a human, rather than returning said inference at said confidence value.

The method of claim 1, further comprising, in an interval between delivery of a response and receipt of a subsequent query, retrieving into a buffer a set of knowledge records predicted from said response and from knowledge records retrieved for preceding queries of a common interaction; serving said subsequent query from said buffer where said subsequent query matches said prediction; and discarding said buffer, without modification to any said knowledge record, where said subsequent query does not so match.

The method of claim 1, further comprising indexing an object classified from a sensor feed by a deterministic mapping from a planar position of said object to a cell of a hexagonal tiling, such that two objects occupying adjacent cells are retrievable as spatial neighbours by cell adjacency alone without a distance computation over their coordinates, and applying an identical said mapping to a position in an embedding space to index conceptual neighbours.

The method of claim 1, wherein said safety classification is a bitmask field of said record schema, is immutable to an application programming interface caller, and is modifiable only in a direction of increased restriction absent a dual-approval operation, such that no code path reads a said knowledge record without also reading said safety classification.

The method of claim 1, wherein said provenance chain is a Merkle directed acyclic graph, said checksum is a keyed checksum, and a mismatch between said checksum and a checksum recomputed over said operation and said safety evaluation indicates that a safety evaluation recorded for said operation differs from a safety evaluation that executed.

The method of claim 1, wherein said plurality of distinct modalities comprises unstructured text, structured data, image, audio, video, sensor data, knowledge graph and code, and wherein content not matching any said modality is classified as unmatched and surfaced, and is not discarded without record.

The method of claim 13, further comprising: detecting that a property of a perceived event is confirmed by two or more of said plurality of distinct modalities within a common temporal window; and assigning a knowledge record constructed for said property a confidence value strictly greater than a confidence value assigned to said property when confirmed by a single said modality alone, wherein a magnitude of the increase is a function of a temporal synchrony between the confirming modality streams.

The method of claim 1, wherein said semantic fingerprint is computed over said canonicalized form after Unicode normalization and independently of a natural language of said content, such that a first said content expressing said semantic assertion in a first natural language and a second said content expressing said semantic assertion in a second natural language yield an identical said semantic fingerprint and converge on a single said knowledge record having two branches of said provenance chain.

The method of claim 1, wherein said threshold function is of the form a_i(t+1) = sgn( Σ_j W_ij · a_j(t) − θ_i ), and wherein a number of distinct stable states said iterative updating is operated to hold is bounded at a fixed proportion of a number of knowledge records of said admitted set, such that convergence to a spurious mixed state is prevented by said bound rather than by filtering a result of said iterative updating.

The method of claim 1, wherein said query is a turn of a multi-turn interaction, and wherein a knowledge record retrieved at a prior turn of said multi-turn interaction is weighted for said retrieving by a factor decreasing monotonically with a number of intervening turns d in proportion to 1/(1+d), and wherein a knowledge record whose said factor falls below a configured floor is released from a working-memory structure without being deleted from a persistent store of said knowledge records.

The method of claim 1, wherein a knowledge record outside said scope description is absent from a traversal of said knowledge records rather than removed from a result of said traversal, such that an existence of said knowledge record is not inferable from a count, a ranking position or an elapsed time of said traversal.

The method of claim 1, further comprising: representing a hypothetical state of said knowledge records as a delta object comprising a reference to a base state, a set of overriding knowledge records and a set of suppressed knowledge records, and not as a copy of said base state; assigning said hypothetical state a probability value; and removing said hypothetical state from evaluation, and discarding said delta object without modification to said base state, where said probability value falls below a configured pruning threshold.

The method of claim 19, further comprising evaluating a single structured query across a plurality of said hypothetical states within one query operation, optionally restricted to a subset of said hypothetical states and optionally weighted by said probability value of each, and returning a result identifying, for each said hypothetical state, the knowledge records within it satisfying said query.

The method of claim 1, further comprising: deriving a synthesized assertion from at least two said knowledge records, said synthesized assertion being stated by no single one of said at least two knowledge records; assigning said synthesized assertion a confidence value not exceeding a least confidence value among said at least two knowledge records; marking said synthesized assertion with a type identifier distinguishing it from an ingested said knowledge record; and delivering said synthesized assertion only with said type identifier preserved in said output text.

The method of claim 1, further comprising evaluating a temporally-scoped rule set incrementally as a said knowledge record is appended, and maintaining a persistent index of contradictions in which an entry is created where two active rules of said rule set yield incompatible conclusions over a common said knowledge record, said index being queryable after delivery of said output text.

The method of claim 1, further comprising, where no knowledge record of said candidate set satisfies said configured threshold, delivering a statement of said boundary together with a nearest available said knowledge record, and not generating said output text.

The method of claim 1, further comprising: identifying a candidate modification to a subsystem executing said method, by monitoring scoped to said subsystem or by a request received from a human operator; evaluating said candidate modification in an isolated simulation environment; applying said candidate modification only upon an approval recorded against an identity of an individual human reviewer together with a stated reasoning of said reviewer; and rejecting said candidate modification where said subsystem is a member of a fixed enumerated set of subsystems, wherein said fixed enumerated set is not modifiable by a candidate modification identified or applied according to this claim.

The method of claim 24, further comprising generating a machine-checked proof of a property of said candidate modification where said candidate modification targets a bounded non-Turing-complete program representation, and presenting said proof to said individual human reviewer as an input to said approval, wherein said proof does not effect said approval.

The method of claim 1, further comprising metering each operation performed in said method as a bounded compute-accounting unit assigned to a category, and scheduling said compute-accounting units such that a unit assigned to a safety-evaluation category is served ahead of a unit of any other category whenever the two contend for a common processing resource, irrespective of an arrival order or a privilege of a requester.

The method of claim 26, further comprising: completing said retrieving, said iteratively updating and said generating before invoking a selection of commercial content; supplying to said selection, as its sole input, a concept identifier resolved from said query together with identifiers of concepts adjacent thereto within one edge of a concept structure, each supplied read-only, said selection holding no write access to said retrieving, said iteratively updating or said generating; scoring a matched commercial candidate as a weighted combination of a relevance factor, an operator-configurable source-priority factor and a bid factor, said weights summing to unity; scheduling a compute-accounting unit of said selection below every unit assigned to said safety-evaluation category; and rendering a selected commercial content in a labeled region distinct from and not interleaved with said output text.

A system comprising: one or more processors; and a memory storing instructions that, when executed by said one or more processors, cause the system to: construct a plurality of knowledge records, each said knowledge record encoding a single semantic assertion and comprising, within a single record schema, a confidence value maintained as a first parameter accumulating evidence supporting said semantic assertion and a second parameter accumulating evidence contradicting it and reported as a ratio of said first parameter to a sum thereof, a safety classification, a semantic fingerprint computed over a canonicalized form of said semantic assertion, and a reference into an append-only provenance chain; construct, responsive to a query received from a requester and before traversal, a scope description bounded by an access entitlement of said requester and by a time interval, such that a knowledge record outside said scope description is not traversable; retrieve a candidate set of said knowledge records from within said scope description and admit into an admitted set only those whose retrieval confidence satisfies a configured threshold; iteratively update an activation value of each knowledge record of said admitted set as a threshold function of a weighted sum of the activation values of the other knowledge records of said admitted set until a stable state is reached; construct a graph structure in which every edge references at least one knowledge record having a positive said activation value at said stable state; and generate output text under a constraint that a permissible output vocabulary at each generation step is limited to terms derivable from said edges, a candidate proposition not so derivable being rejected before output.

The system of claim 28, wherein said instructions further cause the system to place a synchronous safety evaluation gate at each of a plurality of operation layers, such that an entry to the system at a first said operation layer does not avoid a said gate placed at a second said operation layer.

A non-transitory computer-readable medium storing instructions that, when executed by one or more processors, cause the one or more processors to perform operations comprising: constructing a plurality of knowledge records, each said knowledge record encoding a single semantic assertion and comprising, within a single record schema, a confidence value maintained as a first parameter accumulating evidence supporting said semantic assertion and a second parameter accumulating evidence contradicting it and reported as a ratio of said first parameter to a sum thereof, a safety classification, a semantic fingerprint computed over a canonicalized form of said semantic assertion, and a reference into an append-only provenance chain whose nodes each carry a checksum computed over an operation and a safety evaluation recorded for said operation; retrieving, responsive to a query and from within a scope description constructed before traversal, a candidate set of said knowledge records; admitting into an admitted set only those knowledge records of said candidate set whose retrieval confidence satisfies a configured threshold; iteratively updating an activation value of each knowledge record of said admitted set as a threshold function of a weighted sum of the activation values of the other knowledge records of said admitted set until a stable state is reached; and generating output text under a constraint that a permissible output vocabulary at each generation step is limited to terms derivable from edges of a graph structure, each said edge referencing at least one knowledge record having a positive said activation value at said stable state, a candidate proposition not derivable from said edges being rejected before output in favour of a narrower proposition that is so derivable. **Ingestion-time question generation and the author supplemental layer (claims 31–39)**

A computer-implemented method for preparing a digital work for grounded interactive query, the method comprising: receiving, at a portal and bound to a verified author identity, a digital work submitted by an author; performing a rights validation on said digital work and withholding ingestion of said digital work until said rights validation returns a cleared status; extracting from said digital work a plurality of knowledge records, each said knowledge record encoding a single semantic assertion and comprising, within a single record schema, a confidence value maintained as a first parameter accumulating evidence supporting said semantic assertion and a second parameter accumulating evidence contradicting it and reported as a ratio of said first parameter to a sum thereof, a safety classification, a semantic fingerprint and a reference into an append-only provenance chain; generating, before receipt of any query directed to said digital work, a plurality of candidate questions by traversing each said knowledge record together with concept-mesh neighbours of said knowledge record, each said candidate question being answerable by at least one said knowledge record; scoring each said candidate question by a coverage measure computed over the knowledge records from which said candidate question was derived, and retaining in a persistent question index associated with said digital work only those candidate questions whose coverage measure satisfies a configured floor; computing, for each retained question and before receipt of any query, an answer assembled from exactly the knowledge records from which said retained question was derived and from no other knowledge record, assigning said answer a confidence value not exceeding a least confidence value among said contributing knowledge records, and storing said answer as a persistent pre-computed answer record carrying a provenance tag distinguishing it from a directly-ingested knowledge record together with an identifier of each said contributing knowledge record; receiving a query and matching said query against said question index prior to performing a traversal of said knowledge records; returning, where a match similarity of said query against a retained question satisfies a configured threshold and no contributing knowledge record of the corresponding pre-computed answer record has been revised since said answer was computed, said pre-computed answer record together with a citation to each said contributing knowledge record; and performing, where either said match similarity or said revision condition is not satisfied, a traversal of said knowledge records and a generation of a response therefrom.

The method of claim 31, further comprising: receiving from said author, subsequent to said extracting, supplemental content concerning said digital work; converting said supplemental content into one or more knowledge records carrying a tag identifying said knowledge records as author-supplemental and carrying said author as an attributed source; making said knowledge records available to each reader holding an entitlement to said digital work without alteration of the rights validation status of said digital work; and regenerating each retained question and each pre-computed answer record whose contributing knowledge records are affected by said converting.

The method of claim 32, wherein a said author-supplemental knowledge record participates in said generating of candidate questions on the same terms as a knowledge record extracted from said digital work, such that a candidate question answerable only by reference to said supplemental content is generated and is eligible for retention in said question index.

The method of claim 31, wherein a said candidate question generated by traversal across two or more said knowledge records is a question that no single one of said two or more knowledge records answers alone.

The method of claim 31, wherein the citation returned with a said pre-computed answer record identifies the identical set of knowledge records from which said answer was computed, such that an answer returned from said question index is traceable to the same degree as a response generated by said traversal.

The method of claim 31, further comprising marking as stale each entry of said question index whose contributing knowledge record has been revised, and excluding a stale entry from return until said entry has been recomputed, wherein staleness is determined by said revision and not by an elapsed time since computation.

The method of claim 31, further comprising computing, at a time of committing a said knowledge record and before receipt of any query, a forward inference chain enabled by said knowledge record, and storing a conclusion of said forward inference chain as a derived-inference record carrying a provenance tag identifying it as derived, such that a retained question whose answer depends on said forward inference chain is answerable without performing said forward inference chain at a time of said query.

The method of claim 37, wherein said derived-inference record is traceable to the knowledge records whose logical entailment said derived-inference record represents, and is not traceable to a single source passage of said digital work.

The method of claim 31, wherein said question index is scoped to said digital work such that no pre-computed answer record of said question index is assembled from a knowledge record extracted from a different digital work, and wherein the contributing-record set of a said pre-computed answer record is fixed at a time of computation and is not extendable at a time of return. **Retrieval-phase boundary and sampling criticality control (claims 40–44)**

The method of claim 16, further comprising: maintaining a load ratio equal to a number of distinct stable configurations the iterative updating is operated to hold divided by a number of units; comparing, before admitting a further stable configuration, a resulting value of said load ratio against a configured operating ceiling, said operating ceiling being strictly below a retrieval-phase boundary at which stable retrieval configurations of said iterative updating cease to exist discontinuously; refusing said admitting where said resulting value would equal or exceed said operating ceiling; and initiating instead a consolidation of existing stable configurations, wherein said refusing is recorded as an entry in said provenance chain.

The method of claim 40, wherein said configured operating ceiling is set within a first regime in which stable retrieval configurations are global minima of an energy function of said iterative updating, rather than within a second regime, lying between said first regime and said retrieval-phase boundary, in which stable retrieval configurations remain dynamically stable but are local minima while other configurations hold said global minima.

The method of claim 41, wherein operation within said second regime requires a deployment election recorded with an identity of an operator who made it, and wherein absent said deployment election said configured operating ceiling remains within said first regime.

The method of claim 4, wherein said inverse-temperature parameter is exposed as an operator-configurable control having at least a first setting under which said sampling concentrates selection on highest-scoring candidates, a second setting under which said sampling broadens selection across candidates of comparable score, and a third setting under which said sampling approaches uniform selection irrespective of score; and wherein a value of said inverse-temperature parameter in effect for a given generation of candidate hypotheses is recorded in said provenance chain with an identity of the operator who set it, such that said generation is reproducible from said recorded value.

The method of claim 43, wherein no value of said inverse-temperature parameter causes an output of said sampling to be admitted to said retrieving or to said generating of output text, and wherein no process of the system is configured to adjust said inverse-temperature parameter toward any value on the basis of the system's own prior outputs. **Concept inheritance, exception override and inverse traversal (claims 45–49)**

A computer-implemented method for resolving an attribute of a concept in a knowledge system, comprising: maintaining a graph of concept nodes connected by typed edges including a subsumption edge type and an attribute edge type; determining that a first concept node is connected to a second concept node by a subsumption edge and that said second concept node is connected to an attribute by an attribute edge; assigning said attribute to said first concept node by inheritance, together with a tag identifying said second concept node as an origin of said attribute and a depth of said subsumption edge; computing a confidence value for said inherited attribute as a product of confidences of the subsumption edges traversed and a confidence of said attribute at said second concept node, bounded above by a least of said confidences; performing said assigning at a time of traversal without writing said attribute to said first concept node as stored state; and returning, with any output relying on said inherited attribute, a citation identifying said second concept node and said subsumption edges traversed.

The method of claim 45, further comprising: determining that said first concept node asserts a second attribute directly, said second attribute conflicting with said inherited attribute; applying said second attribute to said first concept node and suppressing said inherited attribute for said first concept node and for every concept node subordinate to said first concept node; and leaving an attribute of said second concept node unmodified and inherited by every concept node subordinate to said second concept node that does not itself assert a conflicting attribute.

The method of claim 46, wherein, where a first inherited attribute and a second inherited attribute conflict and are inherited from concept nodes at differing subsumption depths, the attribute inherited from the lesser depth governs; and wherein, where said differing depths are equal, no resolution is performed, an entry is created in a persistent contradiction index, and an output relying on said attribute reports both values together with their respective originating concept nodes.

The method of claim 46, wherein an assertion suppressing an inherited attribute is recorded with an identity of an ingestion event or a reviewer that produced it, and wherein a set of concept nodes suppressing a given attribute of a given concept node is retrievable as a query result.

The method of claim 45, further comprising traversing a typed edge in a reverse direction by resolving an inverse predicate declared in a schema of said edge's predicate at a time of traversal, without storing a second edge representing said reverse direction; and refusing said traversing, and reporting an absent inverse declaration, where said predicate declares no inverse predicate. **Wording-operative spans and idiom equivalence (claims 50–53)**

A computer-implemented method for generating output in a target language from knowledge records, comprising: constructing knowledge records each encoding a semantic assertion and each carrying a language-independent semantic fingerprint; generating output text in a target language by realizing said knowledge records under a constrained vocabulary, without reference to a surface form of a source content from which said knowledge records were constructed; determining that a first knowledge record is marked as wording-operative; reproducing, for said first knowledge record, a source span of said source content in a source language of said source span rather than realizing said first knowledge record under said constrained vocabulary; generating a gloss of said source span in said target language and marking said gloss as non-operative; and exempting said reproduced source span, and no other span of said output text, from a groundedness rewriting applied to said output text.

The method of claim 50, further comprising withholding said reproducing where a rights validation of said source content does not permit reproduction of said source span, and delivering said gloss alone together with an indication that operative wording is not reproducible under an applicable right, wherein a fact extracted from said source content into a knowledge record remains available irrespective of said withholding.

The method of claim 50, further comprising: determining, at a time of constructing a knowledge record from a source span, that a compositional reading of said source span and an attested reading of said source span registered in a concept structure diverge by more than a configured threshold; recording in said knowledge record said attested reading rather than said compositional reading, together with a marking identifying said knowledge record as idiom-derived and an identifier of said source span; and realizing said knowledge record in said target language using a target-language expression registered in said concept structure for said attested reading.

The method of claim 52, further comprising, where no target-language expression is registered in said concept structure for said attested reading, realizing said attested reading literally together with an indication that said source span expressed said attested reading idiomatically, and refraining from selecting a target-language expression on a basis of surface similarity to said source span. **Linguistic resource registry and derived-artifact-only ingestion (claims 54–57)**

The method of claim 12, further comprising: maintaining a registry of externally-sourced linguistic resources consulted by said extraction stages, each registration recording an identifier and version of a resource, a licensor, a licence instrument, a permitted-use scope, a redistribution permission, an attribution requirement, and an ingestion mode; withholding consultation of a resource by any said extraction stage until said resource is registered; refusing registration where said permitted-use scope does not encompass an intended use declared by an operator; and recording each registration and each refusal as an entry in said provenance chain.

The method of claim 54, further comprising associating with each artifact derived from a registered resource a reference to said registration, and enforcing, at each point at which said artifact would be redistributed or exposed, a derivative condition imposed by the licence instrument of said registration; and wherein, where two registered resources impose conflicting derivative conditions on a common artifact, said artifact is marked non-redistributable and said conflict is recorded, rather than being resolved by selection of a less restrictive condition.

The method of claim 54, wherein a resource registered in a derived-artifact-only ingestion mode is consulted to compute an aggregate quantity over said resource, said aggregate quantity is retained, and no span of text of said resource is retained in a knowledge record, an index or a cache, or reproduced in an output; and further comprising verifying compliance by determining that a count of retained source spans attributable to a resource registered in said mode is zero, and surfacing a non-zero said count as a compliance failure.

The method of claim 56, wherein said aggregate quantity comprises at least one of a term frequency, a collocation strength, a part-of-speech distribution and a morphological paradigm, and wherein retention of said aggregate quantity and non-retention of said span implement a distinction between a fact about said resource and an expression contained in said resource. **Session modes, annotation, bounded programs, authoring, immersive presentation, infrastructure and governance (claims 58–107)**

The method of claim 1, wherein said generating is performed in a selected one of a plurality of session modes, each said session mode applying a distinct composition rule to a common said stabilized set, and wherein no said session mode admits into said output text a proposition not derivable from said stabilized set.

The method of claim 58, wherein in a first said session mode a candidate set retrieved at each turn is conditioned on knowledge records accumulated across preceding turns of a common interaction, such that a reference resolved at a preceding turn remains resolved without restatement.

The method of claim 58, wherein in a second said session mode a viewpoint attested within ingested content is adopted for composition, said viewpoint being marked as attributed to said content and not as a position of the system, and wherein a proposition supporting said viewpoint that is not derivable from said stabilized set is rejected.

The method of claim 58, wherein in a third said session mode said stabilized set is ordered into a sequence of instructional steps by a dependency relation among said knowledge records, each said step citing the knowledge record from which it was composed.

The method of claim 58, further comprising generating an assessment item from a target knowledge record of said stabilized set, receiving a submitted response, and scoring said submitted response by a semantic similarity of said response to the content of said target knowledge record against a configured threshold, wherein said assessment item and a lesson delivered in another said session mode are generated from a common set of said knowledge records.

The method of claim 58, wherein in a fourth said session mode said stabilized set is ordered by a temporal anchor field of each said knowledge record, and a knowledge record lacking a temporal anchor is reported as unordered rather than assigned a position.

The method of claim 1, further comprising comparing a first set of knowledge records associated with a first edition of a work against a second set associated with a second edition by traversing a supersession chain of each said knowledge record, and reporting each compared element as changed or unchanged together with the knowledge records constituting each said edition.

The method of claim 58, further comprising deriving from a single said knowledge record a prompt portion and an answer portion of a study item, said answer portion being the content of said knowledge record rather than a restatement of it, and scheduling a subsequent presentation of said study item at an interval computed as a prior interval scaled by an ease factor where a recorded recall quality satisfies a configured floor.

The method of claim 1, further comprising storing reader-authored content as a knowledge record whose access control list determines its visibility, wherein a first said access control list restricts visibility to the authoring reader, a second is set from a sharing configuration declared by an author of the work, and a third is scoped to a class roster held by an instructor, and wherein a reader-authored said knowledge record is distinguished by type from a knowledge record extracted from said work and is not admitted to said stabilized set as content of said work.

The method of claim 66, further comprising routing a submitted post into one of a plurality of discussion partitions determined by a role held by the submitting identity and by a scope of a work or a class associated with said partition, and applying to said post the same safety evaluation applied to a said knowledge record.

The method of claim 1, further comprising condensing an interaction session into a session archive record retained by default at session end, and providing an erasure operation exercisable by the requester at a session scope, a work scope and an account scope, wherein exercise of said erasure operation at said account scope where a reader-held encryption key governs said records is effected by destruction of said key record.

The method of claim 68, further comprising clustering a plurality of said session archive records of a common requester by proximity of an aggregate semantic vector of each, and reporting a concept appearing in session archive records associated with two or more distinct works as a cross-work connection cited to the knowledge records in which said concept appears.

The method of claim 1, further comprising rendering a citation of said output text in a selected one of a plurality of presentation forms comprising a graph rendering of knowledge records and edges within a scope, a preview of a cited knowledge record surfaced without leaving a current view, and an inline dismissible annotation, wherein each said presentation form resolves to the same knowledge record identified by said citation and none introduces a proposition absent from said stabilized set.

The method of claim 1, further comprising compiling a natural-language instruction into a bounded program by decomposing said instruction into operational intents before binding any intent to a concrete entity, binding each said intent to a concrete type and predicate reference by an entity resolution common to said extracting, and halting said compiling and returning a clarification request where a said binding is ambiguous rather than selecting among candidate bindings.

The method of claim 71, wherein said bounded program is expressed in a primitive set comprising a fixed number of read primitives, a single state-changing primitive subject to said safety evaluation, and a single iteration primitive enforcing a runtime iteration ceiling, such that said bounded program is not Turing-complete in an unbounded sense and its termination is enforced by said runtime rather than by convention.

The method of claim 1, wherein said knowledge records are maintained in a committed layer and an in-memory overlay reconciled on a fixed interval, a knowledge record in said overlay carrying a provisional reference into said provenance chain that is finalized and never altered on completion of a durable write, and wherein said retrieving reads said committed layer overlaid with matching entries of said overlay.

The method of claim 73, further comprising registering a said bounded program with a trigger condition, evaluating said trigger condition against each change to said overlay, and re-applying said safety evaluation to said bounded program on each firing rather than only at registration.

The method of claim 1, further comprising accumulating knowledge records incrementally as a draft is edited, versioning each edit through said supersession chain, and detecting a concurrent-write divergence between two authors by comparing a head of said supersession chain held by each, wherein divergence is reported for resolution and neither write is discarded.

The method of claim 75, further comprising evaluating a draft's own knowledge records against one another under said rule set and reporting a continuity defect where two said knowledge records of said draft yield incompatible conclusions concerning a common subject.

The method of claim 75, further comprising constructing from a current state of said draft a hypothetical-state branch represented as a delta object referencing a base state and retaining both said current state and said branch, such that exploration of an alternative does not modify said draft.

The method of claim 1, further comprising accepting a submitted work into a publication workflow, validating a right to distribute said work before any said extracting is performed, and withholding said extracting until said validating returns a cleared status.

The method of claim 1, further comprising serializing every knowledge record to which a requesting identity holds a right into an open interchange format on request, wherein said serializing is not conditioned on a continuing entitlement and no access to said records is withdrawn by reason of said serializing.

The method of claim 1, further comprising generating an accessible-equivalent knowledge record from the same source content and at the same production stage as the knowledge record it accompanies, and reporting a production as incomplete where a said accessible-equivalent record is absent.

The method of claim 1, further comprising inferring a colour value for a region of visual content lacking reliable colour information from a material and lighting classification of said region recorded as a knowledge record, wherein said inferring is deterministic and each inferred colour is traceable to the knowledge record from which it was inferred.

The method of claim 1, further comprising instantiating a three-dimensional rendering of a scene from knowledge records carrying spatial detail, and withholding said instantiating where the spatial detail carried by said knowledge records does not satisfy a configured sufficiency threshold, rather than supplying absent spatial detail.

The method of claim 81, further comprising representing a reference colour as a knowledge record carrying a declared tolerance, and applying a fixed rule set to geometry and constraint knowledge records to produce a geometric conclusion together with a citation of each said record relied upon.
